observations: DESIGN-LEVEL DETERMINISM PASS: All 48 (state, action) pairs have 4 distinct candidates in CANDIDATES design. The SPA is guaranteed to have H(S_next | state, action) > 0 for every stratum by design.

EMPIRICAL DETERMINISM: K2 det_ratio = 0.315 (407/1292 strata deterministic), K3 det_ratio = 0.108 (89/821). The hash function maps different histories to the same candidate, creating deterministic strata empirically despite the CANDIDATES design having all distinct values.

BIAS PERSISTS: All 4 estimators have |shuffled-action null mean| >= 0.1 bits: weighted=0.407, equal=0.704, median=0.686, KNN=-0.262. The bias is REPRODUCIBLE within 0.001 bits of the parent experiment on the same SPA design.

STRATUM-SIZE BIAS DECOMPOSITION: Null bias is monotonically decreasing in stratum size: +0.736 bits at size 5-9, +0.562 at 10-19, +0.369 at 20-49. Small strata carry the bias. Pattern IDENTICAL to parent.
POSITIVE CONTROL: All 4 estimators PASS C3 on 8-state deterministic SPA (K3 >= 1.0 bit, p <= 0.001). Pipeline validated.
NO PHASE 2: No estimator passes C1, so beyond-Markov K3-K2 test and convergence test are not executed.
validity_notes: The CANDIDATES design already had all distinct values in the parent experiment. The '0% deterministic strata' redesign is verified at the design level, but the hash function creates deterministic strata empirically (31.5% at K2) because different (prev1, prev2) tuples hash to the same candidate index.

The bias persists at nearly identical levels to the parent (weighted null_mean 0.407057 vs 0.407), confirming the bias is intrinsic to the plug-in PMI estimator's weighted-averaging across strata of varying size, NOT caused by deterministic/stochastic strata mixing in the CANDIDATES design.

The stratum-size decomposition shows the same monotonic pattern as the parent: +0.736 at size 5-9 vs +0.369 at size 20-49. This confirms the bias is a property of small strata regardless of the CANDIDATES design.
KNN CMI produces negative null bias (-0.262 bits) from Laplace smoothing + extra action dimension, consistent with parent.
N=5000 is adequate per prereg adequacy rule: 30.8% of strata have >= 5 records (398/1292 at K2).
All estimators use identical implementation to parent for comparability.
No browser/network required; in-memory simulation only.
